symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2 in the same VLAN 10, but both have correct IPs.
topology_note: PC1 (Fa0/2) and PC2 (Fa0/4) connected to SW1, both assigned VLAN 10.
show_command_output:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
1 default active Fa0/1, Fa0/3
10 Sales active Fa0/2
20 IT active Fa0/4

SW1# show interfaces Fa0/4 switchport
Name: Fa0/4
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (IT)
expected_fault: Port assigned to wrong VLAN (Fa0/4 in VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10)

symptom: New PC connected to access port cannot get any network connectivity at all, link light is off.
topology_note: PC3 (Fa0/6) connected to SW1 trunk-configured port meant for access.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces Fa0/6 switchport
Name: Fa0/6
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: down
Trunking VLANs Enabled: ALL

SW1# show interfaces Fa0/6 status
Port Status Vlan Duplex Speed
Fa0/6 notconnect trunk auto auto
expected_fault: Port configured as trunk instead of access, causing mode mismatch/down state

symptom: PCs in VLAN 30 across two switches cannot communicate even though VLAN 30 exists on both.
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 connected via Fa0/1 trunk link; VLAN 30 exists on both switches.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port Mode Encapsulation Status Native vlan
Fa0/1 on 802.1q trunking 1

Allowed VLANs on trunk:
1-29,31-4094
expected_fault: VLAN 30 not permitted in the trunk's allowed VLAN list

symptom: All hosts in VLAN 40 lost connectivity after a switch reboot; VLAN 40 no longer appears in VLAN database.
topology_note: SW1 standalone switch, VLAN 40 previously configured for Finance department.
show_command_output:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
1 default active Fa0/1-8

SW1# show flash:
vlan.dat file missing
expected_fault: VLAN database (vlan.dat) lost/corrupted after reboot, VLAN 40 no longer exists

symptom: PC gets a valid IP via DHCP but cannot reach any device outside its own subnet.
topology_note: PC1 (VLAN 10, 192.168.10.10/24) with router R1 as gateway on 192.168.10.1.
show_command_output:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.10
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.100

PC1> ping 192.168.10.100
Request timed out.
expected_fault: Default gateway on PC is misconfigured/wrong IP (should be .1, is .100)

symptom: PC can ping its own gateway interface but cannot reach any remote subnet.
show_command_output:
PC1> ping 192.168.20.1
Reply from 192.168.20.1: bytes=32 time=1ms

PC1> ping 192.168.30.5
Request timed out.

R1# show ip route
C 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0
(no route to 192.168.30.0 shown)
expected_fault: Router has no route to the remote subnet despite reachable gateway

symptom: PC gets 'destination host unreachable' when pinging default gateway.
topology_note: PC1 (192.168.5.20/24) on VLAN 5, gateway R1 sub-interface Fa0/0.5 (192.168.5.1).
show_command_output:
R1# show ip interface brief
Interface IP-Address Status Protocol
FastEthernet0/0.5 192.168.5.1 administratively down down
expected_fault: Gateway sub-interface is administratively shut down

symptom: Two PCs on the same subnet have inconsistent gateway addresses and one cannot leave the LAN.
show_command_output:
PC2> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.1.11
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.1.254

R1# show ip interface brief
FastEthernet0/0 192.168.1.1 up up
expected_fault: PC2 configured with wrong gateway address not matching router interface

symptom: PC shows an Automatic Private IP Address (169.254.x.x) and cannot get a DHCP-assigned address.
topology_note: PC1 connected to SW1 Fa0/3, DHCP server configured on R1 for pool NETWORK1.
show_command_output:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 169.254.12.4
Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway: 0.0.0.0

R1# show ip dhcp pool NETWORK1
Pool NETWORK1 :
No State (pool disabled or exhausted)
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted or disabled, PC self-assigned APIPA address

symptom: New PC does not receive an IP address; DHCP server exists on a different VLAN/subnet.
topology_note: PC1 on VLAN 10, DHCP server (R1) on VLAN 10 interface only; no relay configured on SW2.
show_command_output:
SW2(config-if)# do show run interface vlan 10
interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.10.2 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address configured)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' for DHCP relay across VLANs/subnets

symptom: PC receives an IP address but with an incorrect DNS server, causing name resolution failures.
topology_note: PC1 obtains DHCP lease from R1 pool SALES.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section dhcp pool SALES
ip dhcp pool SALES
 network 192.168.15.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.15.1
 dns-server 8.8.4.4
expected_fault: DHCP pool configured with wrong/unreachable DNS server address

symptom: All PCs on a subnet get duplicate IP address warnings and intermittent connectivity.
topology_note: PC1 and PC3 both received 192.168.25.10 from DHCP pool and a statically configured PC.
show_command_output:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.25.10

PC3> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.25.10

Windows: 'An IP address conflict was detected'
expected_fault: DHCP pool excluded-address range not configured, overlapping with statically assigned host

symptom: PC can ping a server by IP address but browsing to it by name fails.
topology_note: PC1 (192.168.1.10) trying to reach server 'webserver.local' (192.168.1.50).
show_command_output:
PC1> ping 192.168.1.50
Reply from 192.168.1.50: bytes=32 time=2ms

PC1> nslookup webserver.local
*** Request timed out
expected_fault: DNS server unreachable or not configured on PC, name resolution failing

symptom: Users report the wrong website loads when typing a known internal domain name.
topology_note: PC1 querying internal DNS server R1 for 'intranet.company.local'.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section dns
ip dns server
ip host intranet.company.local 192.168.1.99
(actual intranet server is 192.168.1.50)
expected_fault: Incorrect static DNS host entry pointing to wrong server IP

symptom: PC cannot resolve any external domain names, but internal name resolution works fine.
topology_note: PC1 uses internal DNS server R1, R1 configured to forward external queries.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section dns
ip dns server
(no 'ip name-server' forwarder configured)
expected_fault: Internal DNS server missing forwarder for external domain resolution

symptom: One specific PC cannot resolve any names while others on the same subnet work fine.
topology_note: PC4 statically configured; other PCs use DHCP-provided DNS.
show_command_output:
PC4> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 0.0.0.0

Other PCs> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.1.5
expected_fault: Static/manual configuration on PC4 missing DNS server address

symptom: PCs on two different routers' LANs cannot reach each other; each can reach its own gateway.
topology_note: R1 (LAN 192.168.1.0/24) and R2 (LAN 192.168.2.0/24) connected via serial link 10.0.0.0/30, no routing protocol configured.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip route
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0
C 10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
(no route to 192.168.2.0/24)
expected_fault: Missing static route or routing protocol between the two routers

symptom: Remote branch network is reachable intermittently; routes appear and disappear from the table.
topology_note: R1 and R2 running RIP, R1 Serial0/0/0 experiencing physical layer flaps.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip route
R 192.168.2.0/24 [120/1] via 10.0.0.2, 00:00:14, Serial0/0/0

R1# show interfaces Serial0/0/0
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is down (flapping)
expected_fault: Unstable serial link causing RIP routes to time out and reappear

symptom: Static route configured correctly but traffic to remote network is still failing.
topology_note: R1 static route to 192.168.3.0/24 via next-hop 10.0.0.6 (typo, should be 10.0.0.2).
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section ip route
ip route 192.168.3.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.6

R1# show ip route
S 192.168.3.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.6
expected_fault: Static route configured with incorrect next-hop IP address

symptom: OSPF neighbors never form; routers on same subnet cannot see each other in neighbor table.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected on 192.168.100.0/30, R1 area 0, R2 area 1 mismatch.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip ospf interface brief
Se0/0/0 0 192.168.100.1/30

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(no output - no neighbors)

R2# show run | section ospf
router ospf 1
 network 192.168.100.2 0.0.0.0 area 1
expected_fault: OSPF area number mismatch between the two routers on the same link

symptom: Traffic reaches the correct remote subnet but return traffic never comes back (asymmetric routing).
topology_note: R1 has default route to ISP; R2 (branch) missing return static route to R1's LAN.
show_command_output:
R2# show ip route
S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1
(no specific route back to 192.168.1.0/24 via R1)
expected_fault: Missing return route on remote router causing asymmetric/broken path

symptom: PC in VLAN 30 can ping the gateway and same-VLAN devices but cannot reach a server in VLAN 10.
topology_note: R1 performs inter-VLAN routing; ACL 101 applied inbound on VLAN 30 sub-interface.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 101
Extended IP access list 101
 10 deny ip 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
 20 permit ip any any

R1# show ip interface FastEthernet0/0.30
 Inbound access list is 101
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies traffic from VLAN 30 subnet to VLAN 10 subnet

symptom: Web traffic to a server is blocked but ping to the same server works fine.
topology_note: ACL 110 applied on R1 interface facing the server subnet, blocking TCP port 80.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
 10 deny tcp any host 192.168.1.50 eq 80
 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL specifically denies HTTP (TCP port 80) traffic to the server

symptom: After adding a new ACL rule, all traffic through the router stopped, including previously working traffic.
topology_note: R1 ACL 120 newly applied to Fa0/0, intended to allow specific host but ends without explicit permit.
show_command_output:
R1# show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
 10 permit ip host 192.168.1.10 any
(implicit deny all at the end)
expected_fault: Missing explicit 'permit ip any any' at the end, implicit deny blocking all other traffic

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can access the internal file server despite security policy forbidding it.
topology_note: WLAN guest VLAN 50 should be isolated from internal VLAN 10 server subnet; ACL 130 not yet applied.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip interface FastEthernet0/0.50
 Inbound access list is not set

R1# show access-lists
(ACL 130 configured but not applied to any interface)
expected_fault: ACL created but never applied to the guest VLAN interface (missing 'ip access-group')

symptom: Internal PCs cannot access the internet even though the router has a valid public IP on its WAN interface.
topology_note: R1 Fa0/0 (LAN 192.168.1.0/24), Serial0/0/0 (public 203.0.113.5); NAT not configured.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip nat translations
(empty - no translations)

R1# show run | include ip nat
(no ip nat inside/outside statements found)
expected_fault: NAT not configured at all on inside/outside interfaces or access-list

symptom: Internet access works for some internal PCs but not others on the same subnet.
topology_note: R1 NAT using access-list 1 permitting only 192.168.1.0/24 to 192.168.1.127 (half the subnet).
show_command_output:
R1# show run | section access-list 1
access-list 1 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.127

PC in 192.168.1.150 range not matched by ACL
expected_fault: NAT access-list wildcard mask too narrow, excluding part of the subnet

symptom: External users cannot reach an internally hosted web server via the company's public IP.
topology_note: R1 configured for NAT overload (PAT) only; no static NAT/port-forward for the web server.
show_command_output:
R1# show run | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface Serial0/0/0 overload
(no static nat entry for 192.168.1.50 port 80)
expected_fault: Missing static NAT / port-forwarding rule for inbound access to internal server

symptom: PCs briefly lose internet access and 'NAT translation failed' appears intermittently under load.
topology_note: R1 using a small NAT pool of 2 public IPs for PAT overload with many internal hosts.
show_command_output:
R1# show ip nat statistics
Total translations: 4096 (max)
Outside interfaces: Serial0/0/0
Pool NATPOOL: netmask 255.255.255.252
start 203.0.113.9 end 203.0.113.10
(pool exhausted)

symptom: Wireless laptop cannot see the company SSID at all, even standing next to the access point.
topology_note: AP1 configured for VLAN 50; SSID 'CorpNet' set to broadcast disabled.
show_command_output:
AP1# show running-config | include ssid
ssid CorpNet
 broadcast-ssid disable
expected_fault: SSID broadcast disabled on access point, hiding the network from clients

symptom: Wireless laptop sees the SSID and connects, but never gets an IP address or network access.
topology_note: AP1 bridges wireless clients to VLAN 50; VLAN 50 not included in trunk to core switch.
show_command_output:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Allowed VLANs on trunk: 1-49,51-4094
(VLAN 50 missing from allowed list)
expected_fault: Wireless VLAN excluded from the trunk link back to the core network

symptom: Laptop can connect to Wi-Fi but authentication constantly fails with wrong password errors despite correct password.
topology_note: AP1 configured with WPA2-PSK; passphrase on AP does not match documented passphrase given to users.

AP1# show running-config | include wpa
security wpa-psk ascii 0 OldPass123
(users given: NewSecure456)
expected_fault: Mismatched WPA2 pre-shared key between access point and client documentation

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users experience very slow speeds and frequent disconnects, wired users are unaffected.
topology_note: AP1 guest SSID and corporate SSID both mapped to VLAN 50 sharing bandwidth with no QoS/rate limiting.

AP1# show wlan
WLAN Profile Name : Guest-WLAN, VLAN : 50
WLAN Profile Name : Corp-WLAN, VLAN : 50
(no separate guest VLAN, no rate-limit policy)
